title: Money that behaves
description:
Write a class `Money` that stores an amount in whole cents and a currency code:

- `new Money(cents, currency = "USD")`; `cents` must be an integer (`Number.isInteger`), otherwise `TypeError`.
- `add(other)` returns a new `Money`; adding a different currency throws `Error` with a message containing both codes.
- `[Symbol.toPrimitive](hint)`: for `"number"` the amount in units (1250 → 12.5); for `"string"` and `"default"` the text `"12.50 USD"`.
- `get [Symbol.toStringTag]()` returns `"Money"`.
- Objects are frozen after construction (`Object.isFrozen` is true), so nobody can change an amount afterwards.
- `Money.sum(list)` adds up an array of `Money`, returning `new Money(0, currency)` of the first item's currency, or `new Money(0)` for an empty array.
hints: `Object.freeze(this)` as the last line of the constructor makes every object of the class read-only.
`Money.sum` is a `reduce` that starts from a zero `Money` in the first item's currency and calls `add` on each, so mixing currencies still throws.
